investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC via curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser): retained the homepage, the /en/programme aggregate listing page, two independent event detail pages, and the site's own public /sitemap.xml. The aggregate listing page turned out to be client-rendered (a JS-driven filter UI with an empty server-rendered placeholder), but the site's own public sitemap.xml provides a genuine, comprehensive, static discovery path (4,153 /en/programme/... URLs with lastmod dates), and each individual event detail page server-renders a full schema.org Event-family JSON-LD block -- together these fully answer the investigation question at Level 1.

probe_history.reason: The homepage confirmed a Magnolia CMS-backed Nuxt frontend (window.__NUXT__.config exposing mgnl* REST API base paths). The aggregate /en/programme listing page itself renders only a <div class="page-loading-placeholder"> server-side (no event data present without JS), so it cannot be used directly for discovery. However, the site's own public /sitemap.xml (plain static XML, no auth) lists 4,153 real /en/programme/... URLs each with its own <lastmod> date -- a genuine, comprehensive, static discovery path. Two independently sampled event detail pages (sound-base-berlin/praed, a MusicEvent; events/lange-nacht-der-museen-2026, an EducationEvent) each server-render one application/ld+json schema.org Event-family block with startDate/endDate as full UTC ISO instants, name, description, and a fully qualified location (name + PostalAddress). This combination (sitemap for discovery + per-page JSON-LD for facts) fully answers the investigation at Level 1 -- no escalation needed for field extraction. (Two brief, unsuccessful attempts to resolve the Magnolia REST Delivery API paths referenced in the NUXT config directly, e.g. /.rest/delivery/hkw-de/pages/v1/en/programme and /.rest/delivery/hkw-de/pageslist/v1, both returned this site's own 404 page -- irrelevant now that sitemap.xml + per-page JSON-LD already solve both discovery and extraction, so this was not pursued further as a separate Level 2 STRUCTURAL entry.)

venue_reference: Haus der Kulturen der Welt / HKW (cultural venue with a substantial music programme, John-Foster-Dulles-Allee 10, Tiergarten, Berlin)

identity.notes: The homepage's own title ('HKW | Haus der Kulturen der Welt') and every retained event's own JSON-LD location.address.streetAddress ('John-Foster-Dulles-Allee 10, 10557 Berlin') directly confirm official identity and match the venue's well-known Tiergarten address.

site_classification.platform: Magnolia CMS (headless, Java-based; window.__NUXT__.config exposes its own mgnl* REST Delivery API base paths, though direct guesses at those paths were not resolvable) with a Nuxt.js frontend. The aggregate programme listing is client-rendered, but individual event pages are server-rendered with a full schema.org Event-family (MusicEvent/EducationEvent/etc.) application/ld+json block, and the site's own public sitemap.xml provides comprehensive static discovery of every programme page URL.

title.notes: Each event page's own JSON-LD 'name' field.

start_date.notes: Each event page's own JSON-LD 'startDate', a full, unambiguous UTC ISO 8601 instant (with trailing 'Z') -- confirmed on both independently sampled pages.

time.notes: Time-of-day portion of the same JSON-LD 'startDate' -- a real UTC instant, not merely a floating local time.

end.notes: Each event page's own JSON-LD 'endDate' field IS always present, but its meaning varies genuinely by record: for the lange-nacht-der-museen-2026 sample it states a real, distinct multi-hour end ('2026-08-30T00:00:00.000Z' vs a 16:00Z start the prior day); for the praed sample it is IDENTICAL to startDate (both '2026-09-03T17:30:00.000Z'), which reads as the source not actually tracking a distinct end for that record rather than a genuine zero-duration event. A future collector should treat endDate == startDate as effectively 'no real end known', not a proven zero-length event.

venue_location.value: Haus der Kulturen der Welt, Angie Stardust Foyer
venue_location.notes: Each event page's own JSON-LD 'location.name' plus 'location.address.streetAddress' ('John-Foster-Dulles-Allee 10, 10557 Berlin') -- room-level naming (e.g. 'Angie Stardust Foyer') within HKW's single building, consistent with this project's existing room-is-not-a-separate-venue precedent.

source_record_id.notes: The JSON-LD payload itself carries no 'identifier'/'@id' field. Each event's own URL path, as directly and first-party stated in the site's own /sitemap.xml <loc> entry (matching the exact URL fetched and retained for this event), is used as source_record_id -- the same documented URL-slug-as-id judgement already established for Moog Barcelona/LAV in this repository, here additionally corroborated by the source's own sitemap rather than merely inferred from a page's own outbound link.

event_url.notes: Neither event page carries a canonical link or og:url meta tag; the event_url is the exact URL retained (matching its own sitemap.xml <loc> entry).

price.notes: No 'offers'/price field exists in the JSON-LD on either sampled page. The praed page's own body prose separately states 'Free entry' as unstructured text (not a structured field), which is not promoted to a claimed price value here.

blockers.description: sitemap.xml is large (4.6MB, 4,153 /en/programme/... URLs spanning many past years) and mixes DE/EN duplicates and non-event page types (series landing pages, publications, calls for submissions) alongside genuine dated events. A collector must fetch each candidate page's own JSON-LD to determine its real @type/startDate and filter to upcoming events, using <lastmod> to prioritise rather than fetching all 4,153 pages unconditionally.

The aggregate /en/programme listing page is client-rendered and cannot be used for discovery; sitemap.xml must be used instead. This was confirmed by inspecting the raw server-rendered HTML (a loading placeholder, no event cards), not assumed.

reasons: Identity PROVEN directly from the venue's own retained pages.
acquisition_class JSON_LD_EVENT, a resolved, supported class, reached entirely at Level 1.

A CONFIRMED public data path retained for both the sitemap.xml discovery mechanism and the event detail page JSON-LD, with 2 independently real sampled events (different schema.org @types, one with a genuine multi-hour end and one without).
title, start_date, time, venue_location, source_record_id, and event_url all PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE.
end honestly assessed PROVEN but flagged with a caveat when equal to startDate; price honestly NOT_PRESENT -- no fields fabricated.
recommended_family JSON_LD, this project's own existing, already-proven-elsewhere generic family (matching the Moog Barcelona precedent) -- requires no new code family.
No unresolved CRITICAL blocker (2 MINOR blockers documented for a future collector to handle: sitemap filtering, and the client-rendered aggregate list page being unsuitable for discovery).

No offline, dependency-free, no-network parser reproduction has been built or run against the retained fixtures in this investigation task -- per this task's own scope, only the investigation record was produced, not collector/test code -- so gate 9 (a DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION evidence item) is not yet satisfied and READY_FOR_ACTIVATION is not claimed. This investigation is complete and ready for that separate offline-proof/collector-build follow-up step.
